# macdefault — agent interface

A macOS-only Swift CLI for default file associations. No Python or duti runtime.
This document describes version 2.1, JSON schemaVersion 1.

## Workflow

1. Inspect: `macdefault list txt --json`.
2. Pick an installed application's `data.candidates[].bundleID`.
3. Preview: `macdefault set txt --app com.apple.TextEdit --dry-run --json`.
4. Apply: `macdefault set txt --app com.apple.TextEdit --json`.
5. Check `ok` and `data.outcomes[].verified`; inspect again if necessary.

`--app` also accepts an absolute .app path. Quote paths containing spaces. Prefer
bundle IDs taken from discovery instead of guessing display names. App associations
are identified by bundle ID; duplicate installations cannot be distinguished reliably.

Office batches: `macdefault suite microsoft|wps|apple --dry-run --json`, then remove
`--dry-run` to apply. The suite name is one of the three literals, not a pipe expression.
All apps must be installed. `macdefault doctor --json` inspects them and the defaults.

Never launch bare `macdefault`: on a terminal it opens the human menu. Always provide
a subcommand and `--json`. Put flags after the subcommand. `set --json` requires --app.
`--no-input` also disables terminal prompts without requiring JSON. Writes use
NSWorkspace.setDefaultApplication; macOS may require confirmation before it
completes. These flags do not suppress operating-system consent dialogs.

## Output contract

With --json, stdout is exactly one JSON document on success and on ordinary
parse/runtime failure. Do not parse human output or stderr. --help and --version are
plain-text informational exceptions. A force-killed process may not emit a document.

Envelope:

    schemaVersion: 1
    ok: boolean
    command: "list" | "set" | "suite" | "doctor" | "macdefault"
    input?: string
    data?: command-specific result
    error?: { kind: "input" | "failed" | "cancelled", message: string, exitCode: integer }

`input` is omitted on some early failures. `data` is omitted if the command failed
before producing a result. `ok` is false for partial execution failure, but completed
outcomes are still in `data`. Do not assume data exists when ok is false.
Additive fields may appear within schemaVersion 1; ignore unknown fields. A breaking
change requires a new schema version. The old 2.0 unversioned payload is now under data.

### list

    data.ext: normalized extension without the dot
    data.defaults[]: { type: ContentType, application?: Application }
    data.candidates[]: Application

Application: `{ name, bundleID, url }`, where url is an absolute file URL.
ContentType: `{ identifier, extensions: [string] }`.
No `application` field means no current default for that type.
Candidates include all current defaults, deduplicated by bundle ID.

### set / suite with --dry-run

    data.changes[]: {
      extensions: [normalized extension],
      type: ContentType,
      previous?: Application,
      target: Application
    }

No writes, registration, or verification are performed. Planning still reads current
system state. `previous` is absent if no default exists. A previous bundle ID equal to
the target means the association was already correct when inspected.

### set / suite execution

    data.outcomes[]: {
      change: the same change object as the plan,
      state: "changed" | "unchanged" | "failed" | "skipped",
      verified: boolean,
      error?: string
    }

By default changes are verified every 250 ms for up to five seconds of waiting per
content type after the setter completes. This timeout does not cover waiting for
system consent. A verification timeout reports failure even if the write returned success. `--no-verify` skips post-write
checks and reports verified=false. `--fail-fast` stops after the first failure; the
remaining outcomes are skipped. Otherwise later associations are attempted.

### doctor

    data.applications[]: { name, application?: Application, error?: string }
    data.defaults[]: the same extension-status objects as list, with candidates empty
    data.errors: [string]

An optional office app being absent is not itself a command failure. A failure to
query a default is reported in data.errors and makes ok=false.

## Exit codes

- 0: success (including preview or already-correct defaults).
- 1 / failed: app resolution, registration, system write, or verification failed.
- 2 / input: required terminal interaction was unavailable or disabled; supply --app.
- 64 / input: invalid arguments/options; fix command syntax or values.
- 130 / cancelled: interactive selection or Swift task cancelled.

With --json, error.exitCode matches the process exit code. In shell pipelines use
`set -o pipefail`; downstream commands can otherwise hide a failing exit code.

## Scope and repeatability

macOS assigns defaults by content type, not independently by extension. One UTI may
cover multiple extensions (txt and text, for example). Read type.extensions in the
preview to see this scope. Only types directly tagged with the requested extension
are changed; generic base types and conformance ancestors are never written.
An extension may map to several UTIs; all matching specific types are included.

A batch is not a transaction. Successful changes remain if later ones fail. There is
no automatic rollback. Repeating the same request is idempotent when the defaults
are already correct. Execution rechecks each current default before deciding to
write; a preview is not a saved or replayable transaction.

Example shell inspection:

    macdefault list txt --json | jq '.data.candidates[] | {name, bundleID}'
    macdefault set txt --app com.apple.TextEdit --dry-run --json | jq '.data.changes'

A guarded execution consumer:

    macdefault set txt --app com.apple.TextEdit --json | jq 'if .ok then .data.outcomes else .error end'

Use the returned outcomes rather than inferring success from a human-readable line.
